about: The reflection question list (comms spec #reflection-questions): each question once, with its id, the reflection it belongs to (lane or director) and its text. octo-feather-lane reflect reads it; a reflection-missed finding's correction lane changes it. Seeded from issue #230 (body and comments).

questions.text: What did anyone (owner, director, supervisor) catch by hand, for example a stranded worker found by reading its pane, and what would have caught it first?
What took long, was repeated, or was answered from memory where a tool could have answered it?
Which rule or promise the lane touched has nothing that would detect it breaking (absence)?
Which check, eval or report field never fired, or fired wrongly, during the lane?

Which step did an agent (supervisor, worker) perform that is mechanical, i.e. the same inputs always give the same action? Route: make it a command (docs/adr/0008 rung 1); role prose then only says when to run it.
Which code-review or qc finding in this lane is a mistake the writer could have been stopped from making, and which role, skill, template or structure would stop it, not only more review?

What did anything (a review, the director, the owner) catch about this lane after an earlier reflection covered it? Each is a finding of class reflection-missed naming the question to add to this list or reword.
What did the owner have to ask or catch, and what would have caught it first?
What did the director answer from memory where a tool or record could have answered it?
Which director decisions led to rework?
Which in-flight change would have unblocked or sped the most lanes this period, and was it first in merge order before the owner asked?
Which owner questions this period were outside spec accept, merge, a scope-changing decision and owner-held access, i.e. the director's to decide and notify?
What did the owner ask that a factory fact already answered (stranded, waiting, gate time, cost), and which report field would have surfaced it first?
Which code-review finding classes recur across lanes (by frequency), why do writers keep making them, and which role, skill, template or structure would stop the writer, not only more review?
Which step did the director perform that is mechanical, i.e. the same inputs always give the same action? Route: make it a command (docs/adr/0008 rung 1); role prose then only says when to run it.

What did anything (a lane, a review, the director, the owner) catch after an earlier reflection covered it? Each is a finding of class reflection-missed naming the question to add to this list or reword.
